column1: # Every file of GameBuddy.Stardew.Integration.Tests that this project does NOT compile.
# The list exists so the included subset cannot shrink unnoticed: run-nogame-tests.mjs asserts that
# included + this file == the suite directory, and names any file that is in neither. A new test in
# the suite therefore either joins the project (it needs no game) or gets a line here (it does).
# The reason column is the measurement, not an opinion: every type name the compiler could not
# resolve was looked up in what this repository declares. `mod-assembly` means it is declared under
# integrations/stardew outside src/Core (Handlers, Navigation, Sensory, ModEntry, ExecutionManager,
# ...); `game` means it is declared nowhere in this repository, so the game, SMAPI, xTile, XNA or
# LiteNetLib provides it. Reproduce with a compile of the suite against Core only.
# A file's diagnostics can stop at its first unresolved game type, so a name declared in this
# repository may never be printed even though the code uses it. Where a `mod-assembly` row names
# such a name, it was measured twice: compile the file against Core alone, then match the
# identifiers it actually uses (comments and string literals stripped) against the declarations
# under integrations/stardew. A file whose only unresolved names are game names stays `game`.
# `reference-tree` is the other measurement, for a file the compiler ACCEPTS: it compiles against
# Core alone but its source reads the decompiled game under /ref/, which is gitignored, so a hosted
# checkout has no tree for it to read and it cannot run in this lane whatever the compiler says.
# Reproduce by compiling the suite against Core only and checking which survivors name
